text:
maria: quick async standup — SLOs / alerts / oncall followups

What I did yesterday: rolled out the SLO backfill job for kv-cache (completed ~90% of keys). Verified missing windows are being reconstructed in staging.
Blockers: eu-west alert churn is drowning the alert channel; can't triage properly while flood is happening. suspicious spike tied to opportunistic cache evictions during long sequences.
Today: will finish backfill, add tighter dedupe on exporter metrics, and pair with oncall to stabilize alerting config. tagging @lee for handoff.

lee: saw the churn this morning. i pushed a temporary debounce to the alert rule at 02:10 UTC (low-risk) to buy time. watching dashboards now, will revert once kv-warmup stabilizes. can you post the link to the backfill job logs?

maria: logs -> https://logs.redwood.internal/kvcache/backfill/174885 - main error was transient OOMs on the worker group. i added memory padding on the job pod spec as a short-term fix.

derek: quick heads-up — opened PR to suppress duplicate alert signatures and add a 5m grouping window: https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/2124. also updated the runbook with the eviction recovery steps. cc @anya for prometheus rule change review.

anya: reviewed the PR, small nit in the label merge. i patched prometheus rule in staging and applied a temporary suppression for alertname="KVCacheEvictionHigh". rule diff (staging):
```yaml
- alert: KVCacheEvictionHigh
- expr: sum(rate(kv_evictions[5m])) > 5
+ alert: KVCacheEvictionHigh
+ expr: sum(rate(kv_evictions[5m])) > 5
+ for: 5m
+ labels:
+   severity: warning
```
This adds a 5m `for:` to reduce flapping. please confirm oncall sees reduced noise.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0420-7 — Title: eu-west kv eviction alert storm. Priority: P2. Assigned: @lee. Link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0420-7

lee: acknowledged incident. i'm running a canary rollback on the last kd-deploy that touched kv-warmup (will take ~3m). calling @maria for validation after rollback.

maria: ok, on validation duty. if rollback doesn't reduce evictions within 10m we'll escalate to a full rollforward with padding and request increased burst capacity.

derek: tagging some followups for later sprint: 1) add stronger observability for sequence-length distribution (ticket INF-837), 2) add adaptive batch-sizing to reduce peak memory pressure (INF-839). i'll add notes to the incident postmortem.

lee: PR ping — maria, can you take a quick CR on infra change that increases job mem? https://git.redwood/infra/k8s/pulls/447

maria: will review in next 20m.

anya: once noise stabilizes i'll schedule a quiet-window test to validate the new `for:` rule and confirm no silent regressions.

lee: thanks all — no blockers from me after rollback started. will post status update to the incident once we see stability or need rollforward. :thumbsup:
